story: Shakuni, prince of Gandhara and brother of Gandhari, lived at the Kuru court as Duryodhana's adviser. He planned the dice game that cost the Pandavas everything, using dice that seemed to obey his will.
belief: He is remembered as the great schemer of the Mahabharata, and his name is used for any manipulative person. Later folk tales say he was secretly avenging his family, whom the Kurus had imprisoned and starved.
turns: His whole life became revenge and scheming, and it destroyed the Kurus and his own sons with them. He was killed in the war by Sahadeva, the youngest Pandava.
facts: Folk legends say his dice were made from his father's bones, so they never failed him; this is not in Vyasa's text.
Gandhara covered parts of today's Pakistan and Afghanistan.
He has a temple at Pavithreswaram in Kerala.
